bib.title: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models

read.skipped: Appendix model-sample pages (G-I examples) skimmed, not read line by line

question: Can a large language model continued-trained on mathematical and scientific text solve college-level quantitative problems with step-by-step natural-language answers and no external tools?
hypothesis: Training on a high-quality dataset that keeps mathematical notation, plus scale and majority voting, closes the gap on quantitative reasoning benchmarks.
contributions: Minerva: PaLM 8B/62B/540B continued-trained on 38.5B tokens of arXiv and math web pages
State of the art on MATH, GSM8k (no calculator) and MMLU-STEM without external tools
OCWCourses: 272 undergraduate STEM problems with automatically checkable answers
Analyses of failure modes, false positives and memorization

method.summary: PaLM decoder-only models are further trained with the autoregressive objective on math web pages, arXiv and a little general text, then evaluated few-shot with chain-of-thought prompts, greedy or maj1@k voting, checked by SymPy equivalence.
method.task: quantitative reasoning (math, science) with chain-of-thought answers; continued pretraining

datasets.name: Math Web Pages
datasets.source: pages with '<math' or 'MathJax-Element-' in HTML, as of January 2022, English only
datasets.preprocessing: HTML stripped, LaTeX/AsciiMath kept; MathML-only pages (~20%) discarded

datasets.name: arXiv
datasets.source: 2M arXiv papers up to February 2021 in LaTeX
datasets.preprocessing: comments removed; filtered if >75k tokens, >0.6 tokens per character, no \section, or empty

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.split: test; train split used for fine-tuning ablation

datasets.name: GSM8k
datasets.preprocessing: Wei et al. chain-of-thought prompt, no calculator

training.lr_schedule: reciprocal square-root decay continuing the pretraining schedule; then LR dropped 10x and trained 4% additional steps
training.hardware: TPU v4 on Google Cloud; 8B on v4-128, 62B on v4-512, 540B on v4-1024; t5x framework

other.note: Table 2 steps equal extra steps plus 4%

inference.decoding: greedy for one sample; nucleus sampling for multiple
inference.max_tokens: 512 generated; inputs truncated from the left to 1024 tokens
inference.samples: maj1@k with k=256 (64 for 540B) MATH; k=64 OCWCourses; k=100 (40 for 540B) GSM8k; k=16 MMLU-STEM
inference.prompting: MATH 4-shot fixed prompt (Listing 2); GSM8k Wei et al. CoT; MMLU-STEM 5-shot or CoT; OCW 'Final answer: The final answer is X. I hope it is correct.'

parameters.majority_voting: group by final answer, pick most common (majn@k picks n most common)

metrics.name: accuracy (greedy / pass@1)
metrics.definition: final answer matches ground truth after normalisation and SymPy equivalence (simplify difference == 0, 5s timeout)

metrics.name: maj1@k
metrics.definition: most common final answer among k samples

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: solved if any of k samples correct

baselines: published SOTA (GPT-2 on MATH, PaLM 540B maj1@40 on GSM8k, Chinchilla on MMLU-STEM)
eval.protocol: Single run; no seeds or confidence intervals reported. Correctness judged on final answer only, with manual false-positive audit on 100 MATH problems.

availability.data: OCWCourses planned for release; not released at time of writing

limits: No automatic way to verify the model's reasoning; false positives increase with difficulty
No external tools such as calculator or Python
Little control over which capabilities are acquired
No ablation with LaTeX stripped from training data in the text
Single runs, no seeds or intervals
Data contamination checked only by BLEU on 100 MATH problems
